title: Rewrite parts of documentation
description:
The documentation could use some work to make them more user-focused. Right now, they read the way that an LLM would document things for themselves.  They were hard for me to read due to the high information density that may be tangential to the topic being documented. 

While I think that the issue is very broad, here are some examples: 

- `?nested_tune_grid()` talks about "the reproducibility contract" but that is not defined or obvious. Maybe it refers to something in one of the Claude plans?
- Almost all of the `@param` entries are excessively verbose and overly detail-oriented. For the `nested_tune*_()` functions, we should probably inherit the description from the original. `resamples,` and a few others might need qualifications, but these should be handled in the Details section. 
	- A specific example is for `@param object`. This should just be the first sentence. The user does not need to know about the condition class or any other details. 
	- Similarly, `@param param_info` should be about the object that is required. The current docs cover the entire data analysis process, even down to `nested_final_fit()`. 
- The use of `--` and a lot of AI catch-phrases doesn't give the impression that the documentation was written by a human or for a human.
- The examples in the help topics have nested recipe statements. These look like unrolled calls from code that used `|>`.
- The vignette's overuse of "you" reads like Claude is speaking.  

One operational note: the topic files can also benefit from using roxygen2 templates and other tools so that the same text does not need to be duplicated verbatim in different files. 

I'd be happy to submit some PRs to refactor various parts of the docs (after our conference is over). Let me know if you agree or would like contributions.

title: other bias correction estimates
description:
I have an API related to the problem that nestedtune is solving, but uses analytical/non-nested estimates via [_A bias correction for the minimum error rate in cross-validation_](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&as_sdt=0%2C7&q=A+bias+correction+for+the+minimum+error+rate+in+cross-validation&btnG=) [[code](https://github.com/tidymodels/finetune/blob/nested/R/debias_estimate.R)]. 

Would you like that in this package? I could also put it in tune.

title: generalize nesting interface
description:
The current implementation is focused on `tune_grid()`. Eventually, we should be able to apply a nested resampling approach to other functions (e.g., `tune_bayes(),` etc). 

I don't know that we would want to make additional functions that echo `nested_tune_grid()` unless we can avoid a ton of code duplication. 

The prototype `tune_nested()` has [an argument](https://github.com/tidymodels/finetune/blob/nested/R/tune_nested.R#L10-L12) for the tuning function. This might be a good idea since we can use `rlang::call2()` to piece together the call for the tuning function, which would dovetail with #33.

title: save .metrics instead of .grid/.selected for inner work
description:
I'm playing around with `nested_tune_bayes` and want to plot trajectories in the inner resamples. To do that, I get the best initial grid point and the iterative candidates. I'll need metrics for that. 

The size difference isn't that much and this might be a good time to get rid of `.selected` since, with the metrics, a basic `slice_{min, max}` can compute the best on the fly.

title: capture candidate frequencies using a method
description: To assess the variability of candidate selection, we could use an API to generate the selections from the inner resamples. Some word like `consensus()` or `agreement()` would work, or we could use the existing `tidy()` method.

title: Enable passing `...` from the top-level function to the `tune_*()` functions
description: So that we can pass options like `control` to `tune_grid()`

title: Simplify print() methods and add `summary()` methods
description:
The current `print()` method doesn't show users that the results are actually tibbles. 

It would be good to 

- mimic `tune:::print.tune_results()` in the `print()` methods here
- take the logic and annotations in the current `print()` method and put them in a `summary()` (or similar method)

title: Odd bug related to parallel processing
description:
A recipes function could not be found when run in parallel. That's fairly odd since other recipes functions are executed before that AFAICT. `nested_resamples()` calls `tune_grid()` directly. This means the `required_pkgs()` method is run inside `tune_grid()`, and everything is accessible. This is verified by the parallel `tune_grid()` results at the end. 

``` r
library(tidymodels)
library(nestedtune)

rec <- 
  recipe(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars) |> 
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |> 
  step_pca(all_numeric_predictors(),
           num_comp = tune())
wf <- workflow(rec, linear_reg())

set.seed(1)
folds <- nested_resamples(
  mtcars,
  outside = vfold_cv(v = 3),
  inside = vfold_cv(v = 3)
)

set.seed(2)
res_seq <- nested_tune_grid(wf, folds, grid = data.frame(num_comp = 1:3))
res_seq
#> 
#> ── Nested cross-validation results ─────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Outer resamples: 3-fold cross-validation
#> Outer folds: 3 requested, 3 completed
#> 
#> ── Selected parameters ──
#> 
#> ! num_comp: 3, 2, 3 (folds disagree)
#> 
#> ── Estimate (3 of 3 outer folds) ──
#> 
#> rmse (standard): 2.69
#> rsq (standard): 0.813
#> 
#> ℹ A nested estimate describes the tune-and-fit procedure, not a model you can
#>   deploy. Build that with `nested_final_fit()`, and report this estimate as
#>   what its procedure achieves.

mirai::daemons(3)
set.seed(2)
res_par <- nested_tune_grid(wf, folds, grid = data.frame(num_comp = 1:3))
#> Warning in nested_tune_grid(wf, folds, grid = data.frame(num_comp = 1:3)): ! 3 of 3 outer folds failed.
#> ✖ Failed: "Fold1", "Fold2", and "Fold3".
#> ℹ See `x$.notes` for what went wrong.
res_par$.notes[[1]]$note[[2]] |> cat("\n\n")
#> Error in `step_normalize()`:
#> Caused by error in `prep()`:
#> Caused by error in `all_numeric_predictors()`:
#> ! could not find function "all_numeric_predictors"

set.seed(2)
cv_res <- tune_grid(wf, vfold_cv(mtcars), grid = data.frame(num_comp = 1:3))
show_best(cv_res)
#> Warning in show_best(cv_res): No value of `metric` was given; "rmse" will be
#> used.
#> # A tibble: 3 × 7
#>   num_comp .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err .config        
#>      <int> <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl> <chr>          
#> 1        3 rmse    standard    2.40    10   0.310 pre3_mod0_post0
#> 2        1 rmse    standard    2.54    10   0.235 pre1_mod0_post0
#> 3        2 rmse    standard    2.56    10   0.241 pre2_mod0_post0
```

title: Add dplyr compatibility methods
description:
These methods define when a tibble with extra classes should drop down to bare tibbles. For example, if you have a 10-fold CV object from rsample and you delete 1+ rows, it isn't really a 10-fold object anymore. 

tidymodels/tune#221 shows the first PR for this in tune. I would probably mimic what is currently in tune since we've improved some of the loading logic and other aspects.
